$comment: Curated Agent Skills manifest for the newsroom-agent-kit. Default install = the 'core' and 'vendor' sections (37 skills). The 'optional' and 'needsReview' sections are documented but not installed. Canonical destination is %USERPROFILE%\.agents\skills. Nothing here is installed yet; Phase 4 applies it.

userContext.role: community manager and content producer for a media outlet
userContext.note: The platform list comes from the user. It is why the eight platform skills in the 'vendor' section were selected and why no LinkedIn skill was taken.

installPolicy.vendorSkills: A fork maintained in this repository under vendor/skills/<name>. Upstream text was rewritten to remove third-party product assumptions (SEC-07). Each vendored skill carries a PROVENANCE.md. Never overwrite a vendored copy with an upstream copy.
installPolicy.fetchSkills: Copied verbatim from the commit pinned in source.ref. The installer never executes an upstream install script.

selectionCriteria: Permissive license with an explicit LICENSE file at the pinned ref, or an explicit license field in SKILL.md frontmatter. One documented exception: og-image, accepted by the user on 2026-10-04.
Instruction-only for the core: no scripts, hooks, binaries or MCP tool requirements.
No API key, account or paid service needed for core behavior.
Portable Agent Skills layout, no vendor-locked paths.
Distinct job; no two default-install skills compete for the same trigger.
Fits an editorial / media-outlet workflow rather than SaaS growth.

optional.name: scheduling-and-queue
optional.reason: SUPERSEDED (Phase 8, reaffirmed Phase 8B). This was the single most-referenced uninstalled sibling (30 references). Postiz was rejected in Phase 8B; Zernio's Queue API now provides slot configuration, queue preview, next-available-slot and queueing a post against a profile. Do not install it.

needsReview.name: accessibility-audit
needsReview.reason: Requires AccessLint MCP tools in allowed-tools, so it is inert without an external service. The repository also has no LICENSE file. Superseded for now by accessibility-compliance.

rejected.reason: Installs OpenCode skills to ~/.config/opencode/skills, breaking the canonical layout. Default symlink install fails on this machine. Ships telemetry. Requires absent Node.
No LICENSE file; package.json private with no license field. Both are thin pointers that fetch an external handbook at runtime.
Mega-bundle: 4241 files, 1006 code files, 1027 SKILL.md, plus hooks, MCP configs and Docker. Only skills/seo is taken.
248 skills, mostly cloud and AI-training oriented. Two directories extracted.
62 skills, 724 code files, hooks, plugins, services. Also the seed was wrong: it has neither fact-check nor content-calendar.
SaaS and product-marketing frame. Its social skill is named 'social', not 'social-content', and triggers overlap the selected social skills.
Frontmatter requires SCRAPECREATORS_API_KEY, a paid API.
Routes to an SEO CLI and MCP server; 1148 code files for one instruction skill.
Every skill requires the AccessLint MCP server; no LICENSE file.
Every plugin is executable TypeScript inside Cline; jev-browser manages external credentials.
Deliberate redundancy control: one calendar and one hook implementation only.

knownGaps: CMS and editorial publishing workflows: deliberately out of scope. The user confirmed they are not needed. No WordPress-specific or generic CMS skill was selected.
Translation and localization: deliberately out of scope per the user. No portable candidate was found in the sources reviewed.

WhatsApp and Telegram: the user uses them, but no portable, license-clean skill was found. email-and-newsletter covers the owned-channel case. Revisit if this becomes painful. UPDATED in Phase 8B: Zernio provides a WhatsApp Cloud API messaging path and a Telegram bot-token path as an execution backend, but still no instruction skill for writing WhatsApp or Telegram content.
CMS and editorial publishing: the execution path now exists. Zernio's Blogs API covers WordPress.com, self-hosted WordPress and Shopify. Still no editorial skill, by the user's original decision.

About 45 sibling skills referenced by the vendored set are not installed. The global AGENTS.md instructs the agent to treat those references as unavailable and to do the work itself rather than inventing content.

postizRationalisation.$comment: Phase 8 mandatory overlap analysis. Guiding principle: skills do the thinking (strategy, editorial judgement, writing, brand voice, planning, community reasoning, content transformation); Postiz is the execution layer wherever it provides reliable native functionality. Full prose matrix in docs/postiz.md.
postizRationalisation.principle: Skills handle thinking; Postiz handles execution. Do not remove a useful strategy or editorial skill merely because Postiz can publish its output.
postizRationalisation.executionBackendNote: For these skills the thinking half stays and the publishing, scheduling, queueing, media upload and native-metrics retrieval half routes through Postiz for the platforms it covers.
whyNothingWasRemoved: facebook-groups survives because Postiz publishes to a Facebook Page, not a Group.
reply-and-comment-writer survives because Postiz attaches comments to its own posts; it does not reply to arbitrary inbound comments.
email-and-newsletter survives because no newsletter integration is configured. ListMonk exists in Postiz but is unset up.
WhatsApp is absent from Postiz's integration list at the reviewed ref, so it stays manual.
crisis-and-moderation is deliberately never routed through an automated publishing backend; it is high-stakes and human-in-the-loop.
postizRationalisation.agentBehaviour: SUPERSEDED BY ZERNIO in Phase 8B. Kept as the Phase 8 record of the Postiz evaluation. Do not provision WSL2, Docker Desktop or the Postiz stack. See zernioRationalisation for the active behaviour.

postizRationalisation.$comment: PHASE 8 RECORD - SUPERSEDED. Retained unmodified as evidence of the evaluated alternative. Postiz was rejected in Phase 8B because its self-hosted stack cannot run on this machine (3.44 GB RAM, WSL absent). See zernioRationalisation for the active classification and docs/social-backend-decision.md for the comparison. Do not act on this section.
postizRationalisation.principle: Skills handle thinking; Postiz handles execution. Do not remove a useful strategy or editorial skill merely because Postiz can publish its output.
whyNothingWasRemoved: facebook-groups survives because Postiz publishes to a Facebook Page, not a Group.
reply-and-comment-writer survived because Postiz attaches comments to its own posts; it does not read or reply to arbitrary inbound comments.
email-and-newsletter survives because no newsletter integration is configured.
WhatsApp is absent from Postiz's integration list at the reviewed ref.
crisis-and-moderation is deliberately never routed through an automated publishing backend.

zernioRationalisation.$comment: Phase 8B. ACTIVE. Zernio is the selected social execution backend. The Phase 8 principle is unchanged: skills do the thinking, the backend executes. This classification was re-derived independently against Zernio's actual command surface, not copied from the Postiz matrix.
zernioRationalisation.executionBackendNote: Up from seven with Postiz. Three skills changed classification because Zernio genuinely implements capabilities Postiz did not: reply-and-comment-writer, community-management, and batch-content-plan.
changedFromPostiz: reply-and-comment-writer: keep -> Zernio execution backend. Postiz could not read or reply to comments; Zernio's inbox can, across platforms, including reviews for Facebook and Google Business.
community-management: keep -> Zernio execution backend. Belonging and rituals stay as reasoning; broadcasts, multi-step sequences and comment-to-DM automations execute the mechanical parts.
batch-content-plan: keep -> Zernio execution backend. Brief-writing stays; CSV bulk upload with a dryRun flag executes a period's posts.
unchangedDeliberately: crisis-and-moderation stays keep - strategic/editorial. Zernio can hide, pin, like and delete comments, but the skill must NOT use those automatically. High-stakes and human-in-the-loop.
facebook-groups stays no meaningful overlap. Zernio publishes to a Facebook Page, not a Group.
email-and-newsletter stays keep - strategic/editorial. No newsletter integration is configured.
scheduling-and-queue stays replace. Zernio's Queue API has slot configuration, queue preview and next-available-slot, which is the genuine backend.
zernioRationalisation.skillsDeferredReason: The six atomic skills from the official Agent Skills index describe raw REST and duplicate the zernio CLI skill. Each is sha256-pinned in manifest/dependencies.json for a future gap.
zernioRationalisation.knownGapsUpdated: CMS and editorial publishing: Zernio's Blogs API supports WordPress.com, self-hosted WordPress and Shopify. The execution path now exists. This is a capability, not an installed skill: the kit gains the ability to publish articles, not editorial judgement about them.
zernioRationalisation.agentBehaviour: When a task reaches the point of publishing, scheduling, queueing, drafting in the tool, uploading media, reading or replying to comments and DMs, sending a broadcast, or reading native post metrics for a connected platform, use the zernio skill and CLI. If no API key is configured or the account is not connected, say so and stop. Do not fall back to Postiz, Postiz Cloud, or any other backend. Never publish, send, delete, hide or moderate autonomously: stage it, show it, and let the human act.

hyperframesRationalisation.$comment: Phase 8. HyperFrames fills a genuine gap: the installed set has no motion graphics or video composition capability. It is additive and supersedes no installed skill.
hyperframesRationalisation.fillsGap: deterministic code-driven motion graphics and local video rendering
hyperframesRationalisation.agentBehaviour: For motion graphics, kinetic typography, animated data, lower thirds, headline cards, overlays or explainer visuals, route to the /hyperframes router. Render locally. Do not introduce image-generation or video-generation models, hosted renderers or HeyGen Cloud.
